title: Close an E-Toll Account after someone has died
summary: You can close a Transport for NSW E-Toll Account at a Service NSW Centre.
intro:
You can close a Transport for NSW E-Toll Account at a Service NSW Centre.

Note: The spouse or surviving partner may be eligible to transfer the e-toll account.
who_can_apply: Enduring Guardian or Power of Attorney
what_you_need: the tag/s (for an E-Toll Tag Account)
a copy of the will for the person who has died
a completed PDF form – Advice of Death
a letter from a solicitor or the NSW Trustee and Guardian advising that the person has died
in the case of a missing person presumed deceased, a 'Presumption of Death Order' issued by the Supreme Court (original or copy)
one of the following documents (for additional identification)

how_to_steps.text: Pay any outstanding amounts on the account.

internal_links.text: Notify Transport for NSW that a customer has died

faqs.q: Who can close the E-Toll Account?
faqs.a: Those who can close the account include a surviving partner/spouse, the executor of the will, or the Enduring Guardian or Power of Attorney.

faqs.q: What documents do I need to close the account?
faqs.a: You need your proof of identity, the E-Toll Account details, the tag(s), a copy of the will, the completed 'Advice of Death' form, the death certificate, a newspaper death notice, and a letter from a solicitor or the NSW Trustee and Guardian.

faqs.q: What if the person is missing and presumed deceased?
faqs.a: If the person is missing and presumed deceased, you must provide a 'Presumption of Death Order' issued by the Supreme Court.
